focus: Time the cleanse, not the silence.
facts: A successful incense cleanse prevents ordinary hunts for 180 seconds.
There is no unique Spirit appearance or vocal sound.
Cursed hunts can bypass this prevention.
steps: Confirm the incense reached the ghost.
Start the timer when the cleanse lands.
An ordinary hunt before 180 seconds conflicts with Spirit; a longer wait alone proves nothing.

facts: Wraith does not disturb salt, including Tier III during hunts.
It can teleport to a player outside a hunt and leave EMF at the destination.
Its model, visible feet and normal footstep sounds do not identify it.
steps: Place salt across a tracked route.
Use a motion sensor or clear manifestation to verify a crossing.
Repeat and consider an enraged Gallu or a copying Mimic.

Its hunt flicker has unusually long invisible intervals.
Roaming towards a player can produce activity away from the favourite room.
steps: Photograph a visible event before it ends.
Check the registered photo and continuing event, not just an empty frame.
Compare several hunt flickers when visibility permits.

facts: Its ability can throw several nearby objects together.
It throws available objects more consistently during hunts.
A single strong throw is only supporting information.
steps: Build a pile of loose props in the activity area.
Watch for one simultaneous burst rather than successive ordinary throws.
Record the sequence and check evidence against The Mimic.

Compare a suspected call with the contextual recording.
Treat ordinary sounds or silence as inconclusive.

facts: Its special 2.5 m/s chase needs a powered breaker, a visible target and more than 3 metres of separation.
It cannot directly switch the breaker off; light overloads can still do that.
Chase acceleration can accumulate behind the special speed.
steps: Record breaker state and target distance.
Compare the chase with the breaker on and off.
Separate direct breaker interaction from an overload.

facts: It cannot turn room light switches on.

Its usual threshold depends on the room's switch state: 60% off, 40% on; equipment lights do not count.
steps: Watch an actual room switch, not just a dark room.
Leave at least 10 seconds between switch changes when repeating the test.
A single quick switch-off can be a coincidence.

facts: It travels at 1 m/s while undetected and 3 m/s after detecting a player.

It keeps the fast pace to the last detection point before slowing.
steps: Listen from a hiding position with electronics off.
Compare a later detection sequence with an escape route ready.
Do not expect it to slow the instant line of sight breaks.

Activity in your room may originate from a ghost in the adjacent room.

Exclude player touches, event closures and locker-door exceptions.

Distinguish an actual mist ball from a manifestation that hisses.

Keep a crucifix in range and note which protection is used.

facts: It tracks players through hiding and slows sharply at close pathfinding distance.

Prepare a looping route before any hunt observation.
Keep moving around it rather than hiding in a dead end.

media.author: Madixx
media.context: Creator demonstration. Compare the recording with the current field notes; older footage can reflect earlier mechanics.

facts: Time spent near players can lower its future hunt speed and activity.

media.context: Creator demonstration. Compare the recording with the current field notes; older footage can reflect earlier mechanics.

Compare stillness and movement from a protected position.

media.author: Madixx
media.context: Creator demonstration. Compare the recording with the current field notes; older footage can reflect earlier mechanics.

focus: Keep a record of protection use.
facts: Salt, a crucifix burn or incense can push it towards its enraged state.
An enraged Gallu ignores salt and becomes weakened after that hunt ends.
Its three states change speed, hunt threshold and protection effectiveness.
steps: Note its state before and after each protection event.
Leave time for salt or incense state changes to apply.
Use the host's salt observation when multiplayer visuals disagree.

media.author: Madixx
media.context: Creator demonstration. Compare the recording with the current field notes; older footage can reflect earlier mechanics.

facts: It starts calm, switches after the first minute, then every two minutes from the first exit-door opening.

A hunt begun aggressive is 20% shorter, even if it later becomes calm.
steps: Log when the investigation door first opens.
Compare several hunt starts and any mid-hunt pace change.
Allow for difficulty, cursed hunts and kills when measuring duration.

media.title: Obambo · guide chapter
media.author: Madixx
media.context: Creator demonstration. Compare the recording with the current field notes; older footage can reflect earlier mechanics.

facts: Its base pace is 1.53 m/s, but chase acceleration builds faster than normal.
Reaching a detected player in an available official hiding place can end its hunt.
It then heads towards that previous hiding location on the next hunt.
steps: Identify an available game-defined hiding place.
Record the approach and whether the hunt ended early.
Furniture corners and blocked hiding spots do not qualify.

media.author: hydrasung
media.context: Creator demonstration. Compare the recording with the current field notes; older footage can reflect earlier mechanics.

facts: It can detect player footsteps, with longer ranges for sprinting than crouch-walking.
It gains visual detection only from moving players within 5 metres.
Standing still does not prevent a collision kill.
steps: Stay out of its likely path and stop voice and electronic cues.
Compare its response to movement on the same floor.
Check for freezing before choosing it over an orb-producing Mimic.

media.title: Kormos explained
media.author: hydrasung
media.context: Creator demonstration. Compare the recording with the current field notes; older footage can reflect earlier mechanics.

facts: It starts at 3 m/s and loses 0.1 m/s per qualifying unique object touched outside hunts, down to 0.4 m/s.
Equipment, doors and cursed possessions do not count; ordinary props and switches can.
A hunt ending or crucifix burn resets the counter.
steps: Interact with multiple distinct qualifying objects before a hunt.
Listen for a lower fixed pace without chase acceleration.
Repeat after the reset; moving one object repeatedly is not equivalent.
